title: Cocartesian-arrow projection is a trivial Kan fibration onto its full vertex image
statement:
Use quasicategories, full simplicial subcategories, products, pullbacks and internal functor simplicial sets from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and trivial Kan fibrations from [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, and let $Y\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$ be the full simplicial subset whose vertices are the $p$-cocartesian edges. Put
$$R=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}E,$$
where the map from $E$ to $B$ is $p$. The simplicial map $\theta:Y\to R$ sends an arrow $u$ to $(pu,u(0))$. Let $Z\subseteq R$ be the full simplicial subset spanned by those vertices $(\alpha,x)$ for which there exists a $p$-cocartesian edge with source $x$ and image $\alpha$. Then $\theta:Y\to Z$ is a trivial Kan fibration: it is surjective on vertices and lifts every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$, with exact agreement on the boundary and over $Z$. No existence of cocartesian lifts for vertices outside $Z$ is assumed.
